questions.question: Which of the following national park is inscribed in UNESCO's World Heritage List (Natural) as of September, 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Keoladeo National Park.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Keoladeo National Park is inscribed in UNESCO's World Heritage List (Natural) as of September 2020.**
 
• Keoladeo National Park is located in Bharatpur, Rajasthan.
 
• It is formerly known as the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary.
 
• This site was declared the UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.
 
• It became a bird sanctuary in 1956 and was declared a national park in 1981.
 
• It was renamed Keoladeo for the ancient temple in the park dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva.

questions.question: Which of the following was built by Muhammed Quli Qutub Shah?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Char Minar.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charminar was built by Muhammad Quli Qutub Shah.**
 
• The Charminar is a monument and mosque located in** Hyderabad, Telangana, constructed in 1591.**
 
• The fifth ruler of the Qutub Shahi dynasty, Muhammad Quli Qutub Shah, built the Charminar after shifting his capital from Golkonda to the newly formed city of Hyderabad.
 
• **Architect: Mir Momin Astarawadi.**
 
• Situated on the east bank of the** Musi river.**
 
• Charminar is also a site of festival celebrations, such as** Eid-ul-Adha and Eid al-Fitr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Quli Qutub Shah (1580-1612)__:**

 __
 
• He was the** fifth sultan of the Qutub Shahi dynasty of Golkonda.**
 
• He founded the city of** Hyderabad**, in** South-central India and built its architectural centerpiece, the Charminar.**
 
• He founded the city of** Hyderabad and named it Bhagyanagar after his Hindu mistress Bhagamati.**
 
• The Charminar was built by him, in **1591 to commemorate the end of the plague in the city, in Indo Islamic style of architecture.**
 
 
 
• **​The Gol Gumbad (Gumbaz)__:**
 __
 
• **​The Gol Gumbad (Gumbaz) of Bijapur is the mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah.**
 
• Gol Gumbaz is the most famous monument in Vijayapura or Bijapur.
 
• This mausoleum of Muhammed Adil Shah was constructed in **1656 by architect Yaqut of Dabul.**
 
• Its most arresting features are the seven-storied octagonal spires at the four corners and the heavy bracketed cornice below the parapet.
 
• It is the **second-largest dome ever built, next in size only to St Peter's Basilica in Rome.**
 
• A particular attraction in this monument is the central chamber, where every sound is echoed seven times.
 
• Another attraction at the Gol Gumbaz is the Whispering Gallery, where even minute sounds can be heard clearly 37 meters away.
 
 
 
• **Buland Darwaza__:**
 
 
• Akbar commissioned the construction of a white marble tomb for Shaikh Salim Chishti next to the majestic Friday mosque at Fatehpur Sikri.
 
• The Mosque is also known as **Jama Masjid.**
 
• **The gateway to this tomb is known as Buland Darwaza (The door of victory).**
 
• It was built in** 1575 A.D.** to commemorate Akbar's victory over Gujarat.
 
• **Buland Darwaza is the highest gateway in the world and is an example of Mughal architecture.**

questions.question: In which of the following states is Bishnupur, famous for terracotta temples, located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

Key Points__**

__
 
• Bishnupur is a city and a municipality in the Bankura district in the state of West Bengal.
 
• It is famous for its terracotta temples built by the Malla rulers, Shree Krishna Raasleela, and the Baluchari sarees.
 
• Since 1997, the temples of Bishnupur is on the UNESCO World Heritage Site's Tentative list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This is embodied in an international treaty called the Convention concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, adopted by UNESCO in 1972.
 
• India has 40 world heritage sites that include 32 Cultural properties, 7 Natural properties, and 1 mixed site.

questions.question: Chand Minar at Daulatabad is a 210-feet-high tapering tower divided into _____ storeys.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chand Minar** is located at **Daulatabad Fort**, situated in the Indian state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is a **210-feet-high tapering tower**, making it one of the tallest towers in the country.
 
• The tower is divided into **four storeys**, each adorned with **decorative balconies**.
 
• It is constructed of **red sandstone** and is an excellent example of the blend of **Persian and Indian architectural styles**.
 
• The Chand Minar was built in the **15th century** by **Ala-ud-din Bahmani** to commemorate his conquest of the fort.
 
• It serves as a significant **historical monument** and showcases the **engineering brilliance** of the medieval period.
 
• The tower also had a functional purpose, serving as a **watchtower** and a symbol of victory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Daulatabad Fort**__

 __
 
• The **Daulatabad Fort** is located near **Aurangabad** in Maharashtra.
 
• It was originally known as **Devagiri**, meaning "Hill of Gods."
 
• The fort is known for its **defensive architecture**, including its **moats, steep slopes, and maze-like entry paths**.
 
• It was briefly the capital of the Delhi Sultanate under the rule of **Mohammed bin Tughlaq**.
 
 
 
• **Ala-ud-din Bahmani**__
 
 
• He was a ruler of the **Bahmani Sultanate**, which was based in the Deccan region of India.
 
• Ala-ud-din Bahmani is known for his contributions to **art and architecture** during his reign.
 
• The Chand Minar is one of his most famous architectural achievements.

questions.question: The famous Dhamek Stupa is located in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhamek Stupa** is a massive stupa located in Sarnath, near Varanasi in **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It is believed to be the spot where Buddha gave his first sermon after attaining enlightenment.
 
• The stupa is about 43 meters high and 28 meters in diameter at the base.
 
• The lower part of the stupa is made of stone, while the upper part is made of brickwork.
 
• The stupa has undergone several renovations over the centuries and is considered to be an important pilgrimage site for Buddhists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Andhra Pradesh is a state in southern India and is known for its rich cultural heritage and historic monuments such as Charminar and Golconda Fort.
 
• Madhya Pradesh is a state in central India and is known for its rich biodiversity and wildlife reserves such as Kanha and Bandhavgarh National Parks.
 
• Himachal Pradesh is a state in northern India and is known for its scenic beauty and hill stations such as Shimla and Manali.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is a state in northern India and is known for its rich history and cultural heritage. It is home to several important pilgrimage sites such as Varanasi, Ayodhya, and Mathura.

questions.question: The national animal of Nepal is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cow is officially recognized as the **national animal of Nepal**.
 
• In Nepal, the cow holds a sacred status, particularly in **Hindu culture**, where it is revered as a symbol of prosperity and motherhood.
 
• The cow was declared the national animal of Nepal in **2015** after the promulgation of the new constitution.
 
• The constitution of Nepal prohibits the **slaughter of cows**, emphasizing its cultural and religious importance.
 
• The cow is deeply integrated into Nepalese traditions and is celebrated during the festival of **Tihar**, where it is worshipped as part of the festivities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Significance of Cows in Hinduism:**

 
 
• Cows are considered sacred in Hinduism and are often referred to as "Gau Mata" (Mother Cow).
 
• They are associated with various deities, particularly Lord Krishna and Goddess Lakshmi.
 
• The cow is a symbol of **non-violence** and nurturing, representing wealth and abundance.
 
 
 
• **Nepal's Constitution and Cow Protection:**
 
 
• Nepal's constitution explicitly prohibits the slaughter of cows, making it a punishable offense.
 
• This legal protection aligns with the religious sentiments of the majority Hindu population.
 
 
 
• **Other National Symbols of Nepal:**
 
 
• National bird: Himalayan Monal (Danphe).
 
• National flower: Rhododendron (Lali Gurans).
 
• National flag: The unique double-triangle flag of Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Tihar Festival:**
 
 
• Tihar is a major Hindu festival celebrated in Nepal, also known as the festival of lights.
 
• One of the days is dedicated to cow worship, where cows are adorned with garlands and offered food.

questions.question: In which state is the Sanchi Stupa situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is located in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• Sanchi is a UNESCO World Heritage site and is famous for its Great Stupa, which is **one of the oldest stone structures in India**.
 
• The Stupa was originally commissioned by the emperor **Ashoka the Great** in the **3rd century BCE**.
 
• The site is a significant Buddhist pilgrimage destination and is renowned for its intricate carvings and historical significance.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is located near the town of **Raisen** in Madhya Pradesh and is approximately 46 kilometers from the state capital, Bhopal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Sanchi Stupa is a major tourist attraction and draws visitors from all over the world.
 
• The site includes several other stupas, temples, monasteries, and pillars, which were added over the centuries by various patrons.
 
• The gateways and railings of the Stupa are adorned with detailed carvings depicting scenes from the life of the Buddha and various Jataka tales.
 
• Sanchi provides insights into the early development of Buddhist art and architecture in India.
 
• The site is maintained by the** Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, which has undertaken extensive restoration work to preserve its heritage.
